The company Greenhouse asked 1,347 people who hire workers. They live in the US, the UK, Germany, Australia and Ireland.

paragraphs: Finding a new job is getting harder. According to a new international survey, only about one in every 20 job applications reaches the interview stage.
The survey was carried out by Greenhouse, a company that makes software for hiring. It asked 1,347 recruiters and hiring managers in the US, the UK, Germany, Australia and Ireland.

Employers say they now receive far more applications than their staff can read. Because of this, many companies use artificial intelligence, or AI, to filter applications. Most applications are rejected by these AI systems before a person ever looks at them.

There is another problem. Many applicants now use AI to write their CVs and cover letters, and these often include false claims about their skills. Almost 90% of the managers admitted they had probably rejected real applications because they believed AI had written them.

AI is also doing more interviews. At the moment, 41% of the managers use it for first interviews, and this is expected to rise to 63% next year. However, almost half say they are adding human checks earlier. Greenhouse's chief executive, Daniel Chait, says people must still be responsible for hiring decisions.
sentZh: 找新工作越來越難。
根據一項新的國際調查，每20份求職申請中只有大約一份能進入面試階段。
這項調查由製作招聘軟體的Greenhouse公司進行。
它詢問了美國、英國、德國、澳洲和愛爾蘭的1,347位招募人員和招聘經理。
雇主表示，他們現在收到的申請遠多於員工能看完的數量。
因此，許多公司使用人工智慧（AI）來篩選申請。
大多數申請在有人看過之前就被這些AI系統拒絕了。
還有另一個問題。
許多求職者現在用AI寫履歷和求職信，其中常含有關於自身技能的不實說法。
將近90%的經理承認，他們可能因為以為是AI寫的而拒絕了真實的申請。
AI也在進行更多面試。
目前41%的經理用它進行初次面試，預計明年將升至63%。
不過，將近一半表示他們正更早加入人工檢查。
Greenhouse執行長丹尼爾．柴特說，人仍必須為招聘決定負責。

paragraphs: Only around one in 20 job applications now makes it to the interview stage, according to an international survey of employers, with the vast majority screened out by artificial intelligence.

The research, compiled by the hiring platform Greenhouse, gathered responses from 1,347 recruiters and hiring managers in the US, the UK, Germany, Australia and Ireland. It found that application numbers have grown so large that staff can no longer deal with them in the traditional way.

As a result, firms are increasingly relying on AI tools to sort candidates, and most applications are filtered out automatically before anyone reads them. Meanwhile, many jobseekers are using AI to write their CVs, and managers say these documents often contain inaccurate claims about qualifications.
This creates a problem of trust. Almost 90 per cent of respondents admitted they had probably turned down genuine applications because they suspected they were AI-generated.
